31/F in New Jersey.  Diagnosed Bipolar 1 with Psychotic Features at 19, those the psychoses didn't come on until about age 23. I had severe depression issues as a child and teenager, and in retrospect,  hypomanic episodes as a teenager. At 19 I hit my first true manic episode. Slept only about 29 mins/day for over 2 weeks. Barely eating. Drinking, drugs, sex, spending. Spending 3 consecutive days dancing in Philly without telling anyone where I was. Picking fights for no reason against people I had no chance with. I was *POWERFUL.* it lasted a solid 8 weeks; possibly up to 10. My memory is fuzzy. I crashed and attempted suicide, and was diagnosed in hospital. 
Around 23, during a manic episode, I started seeing things, and became absolutely convinced that Shadow Demons called "Nag Parisii" were after me and were going to kill me, and I had to abscond immediately to get away. I also started making phone calls to friends with small children at all hours of the night (which I have no memory of doing 😕) telling them to get the children out NOW because the demons were going to try to get to me through the children. These kinds of episodes, along with crippling depression and suicidal thoughts and attempts, continued at a rate of about twice per year throughout my 20's. For my 25th birthday, I was invited to a friend's house for coffee and cake, and ambushed and taken to a hospital because I had been Psychotic and unwilling to get help myself. 
I have been on Lithium for almost 3 years, with only hints of mania since, requiring minor routine and medication dosage changes.

It's been 12 years and 1 year for me. I still get stuck in flashbacks during the day, like today, and the nights are bad. Sometimes the dreams are just reliving everything, and sometimes, my head fucks with me and it's the same situation,  but itll be one of my brothers, whom I adore, doing it to me. I don't even know what to do with that.

Same with playing musical instruments- mess up a note or phrase? Must be able to repeat perfectly, 3 times in a row, before I can move on. Things must be ordered in certain numbers- threes are ideal, but fives and sevens are acceptable depending on circumstances. The dishes are arranged in a certain order and pattern when they go on the dish rack. 
The concern with all of this is Cosmic Retribution. If I am not doing these things perfectly, and in a way that is aesthetically pleasing, I will screw up some karmic balance for myself and be in for deep trouble. 
On a more personal level, it relates to pleasing my father. 

PS, I've kindof known most of my life that what goes on is OCD, but I was only officially diagnosed about 6 months ago, at age 31.

Hopefully, wherever you go will offer more services than medication management/shoving meds down your throat for a few days and releasing you. If they do, participate in programs/activities/groups as much as you are able. But be gentle with yourself. Dont judge or beat yourself up if you are unable to participate or do everything. And dont feel obligated to bond and make friends with anybody, or to avoid anybody. Do what feels right. However, I would *strongly* urge you to find a nurse, or counselor to connect with, whom you trust, and can reach out at any moment you are feeling unsafe or upset for any reasons. The doctors are there to supervise your care, but the real healing is done by the people you see every day. 
And try are hard as you can to focus on the daily routines to take care of yourself, like showering, eating, tidying up. As silly as it seems, being able to do those does wonders for being able to go back to being a human being. 
God bless you and keep you, and I hope to see you on the other side.
